label: copy phase, from the 3rd output onward (diffuse, token-modulated)
explanation: Almost entirely a copy-phase feature: 99% of activation mass is at copy steps (t > L). It is essentially silent during the original tokens and on <DEL>, and weak on the first copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, rate 8%). The firing rate peaks at recall_idx 3-4 (about 40%) and is higher in the last ~4 outputs of a sequence (to_go <= 3). Within the copy phase it fires on only about 25-30% of steps, and which steps depends on content. The output token matters most: o (58% rate), t, r, x and n fire much more often than other tokens. The top activations are short sequences (L=4-5) whose output is o, e.g. at t e o o r <DEL>. The predicate phase==2 & recall_idx>=2 covers about 94% of active steps and 95% of mass but has only about 31% precision. Adding a token set or position windows raised precision but cost recall, and no predicate passed F1 0.49.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=9: 1, a, o, x; t=11: o, 1, a, j; t=13: o, 1, a, j) and the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: o, t, n, x; copy phase: o, t, r, x; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4.
